Introdução:

A

hiperferritinemia

é

um

achado

frequente

na

prática

clínica

e

possui

etiologias

diversas,

que

incluem

desde

processos

inflamatórios

e

metabólicos

até

sobrecarga

férrica

verdadeira

genética,

como

na

hemocromatose

hereditária

(HH).

No

Brasil,

a

heterogeneidade

étnica

e

a

variação

regional

na

prevalência

das

mutações

do

gene

HFE

podem

modificar

a

expressão

fenotípica

da

doença,

tornando

fundamental

compreender

como

marcadores

laboratoriais

e

genótipos

se

comportam

em

populações

miscigenadas.


Objetivo:

Este

estudo

teve

como

objetivo

descrever

o

perfil

clínico,

laboratorial

e

genético

de

pacientes

investigados

entre

2010

e

2024

por

suspeita

de

sobrecarga

de

ferro

em

um

hospital

universitário

do

sul

do

Brasil,

analisando

diferenças

entre

portadores

e

não

portadores

de

mutações

HFE,

comparando

genótipos,

padrões

de

zigosidade

e

avaliando

influência

do

sexo

nos

desfechos

laboratoriais.


Metodologia:

Trata-se

de

um

estudo

retrospectivo

com

278

pacientes

investigados

entre

2010

e

2024.

Foram

analisadas

variáveis

demográficas,

laboratoriais,

presença

de

comorbidades

e

genótipos

HFE.

Comparações

foram

realizadas

conforme

sexo,

tipo

de

mutação

e

padrão

de

zigosidade,

utilizando

testes

não

paramétricos.


Resultados:

Entre

os

indivíduos

avaliados,

54%

apresentavam

mutação

no

HFE,

sendo

os

genótipos

mais

frequentes

H63D/WT

(23,7%)

e

C282Y/C282Y

(10,8%).

Homens

foram

diagnosticados

mais

precocemente

(55

vs.

60

anos;

p

<

0,01)

e

apresentaram

ferritina

significativamente

mais

elevada

(950

vs.

609

ng/mL;

p

=

0,03).

A

homozigose

C282Y

exibiu

fenótipo

mais

expressivo,

com

saturação

da

transferrina

mediana

de

88%.

Os

grupos

H63D/WT

e

WT/WT

demonstraram

perfis

laboratoriais

semelhantes,

reforçando

que

hiperferritinemia

significativa

pode

ocorrer

mesmo

na

ausência

de

variantes

HFE.

A

ferritina

não

discriminou

genótipos

(p

=

0,465).

A

análise

por

zigosidade

revelou

tendência

de

maior

ferritina

em

homozigotos

(p

=

0,057)

e

diferenças

marcantes

na

saturação

da

transferrina

(p

<

0,001).

A

ressonância

magnética

demonstrou

sobrecarga

hepática

grave

predominantemente

em

homozigotos

C282Y.


Conclusão:

Os

achados

deste

estudo

ampliam

o

entendimento

da

hiperferritinemia

em

nossa

população,

alinhando-se

em

grande

parte

à

literatura

internacional,

especialmente

quanto

à

maior

expressividade

clínica

dos

homens

e

à

associação

entre

a

homozigose

C282Y

com

níveis

elevados

de

ferritina

e

saturação

da

transferrina.

Contudo,

diferenças

relevantes

emergiram

ao

compararmos

com

estudos

europeus,

a

maior

expressividade

fenotípica

de

8

da

de

mutações

relevantes

mesmo

em

pacientes

com

saturação

da

transferrina

inferior

a

40%.

Tais

particularidades

podem

refletir

a

composição

genética

diversa

do

sul

do

Brasil,

como

influências

ambientais

e

culturais.

Assim,

os

resultados

reforçam

a

necessidade

de

uma

avaliação

clínica

e

laboratorial

mais

sensível

e

integrada

para

suspeita

de

hemocromatose

hereditária,

para

reduzir

o

subdiagnóstico

e

orientar

adequadamente

as

condutas.

ABSTRACT:


Title:

Epidemiological

profile

of

patients

evaluated

for

suspected

iron

overload:

a

14-year

analysis

in

a

referral

center

in

Southern

Brazil


Introduction:

Hyperferritinemia

is

a

frequent

finding

in

clinical

practice

and

has

diverse

etiologies,

ranging

from

inflammatory

and

metabolic

processes

to

true

genetic

iron

overload,

such

as

hereditary

hemochromatosis

(HH).

In

Brazil,

ethnic

heterogeneity

and

regional

variation

in

the

prevalence

of

HFE

gene

mutations

may

modify

the

phenotypic

expression

of

the

disease,

making

it

essential

to

understand

how

laboratory

markers

and

genotypes

behave

in

admixed

populations.


Objective:

This

study

aimed

to

describe

the

clinical,

laboratory,

and

genetic

profile

of

patients

investigated

between

2010

and

2024

for

suspected

iron

overload

at

a

university

hospital

in

southern

Brazil,

analyzing

differences

between

carriers

and

non-carriers

of

HFE

mutations,

comparing

genotypes

and

zygosity

patterns,

and

assessing

the

influence

of

sex

on

laboratory

outcomes.


Methods:

This

was

a

retrospective

study

including

278

patients

investigated

between

2010

and

2024.

Demographic

variables,

laboratory

parameters,

comorbidities,

and

HFE

genotypes

were

analyzed.

Comparisons

were

performed

according

to

sex,

mutation

type,

and

zygosity

pattern

using

non-parametric

tests.


Results:

Among

the

individuals

evaluated,

54%

carried

an

HFE

mutation,

with

the

most

frequent

genotypes

being

H63D/WT

(23.7%)

and

C282Y/C282Y

(10.8%).

Men

were

diagnosed

earlier

(55

vs.

60

years;

p

<

0.01)

and

had

significantly

higher

ferritin

levels

(950

vs.

609

ng/mL;

p

=

0.03).

C282Y

homozygosity

exhibited

the

most

expressive

phenotype,

with

a

median

transferrin

saturation

of

88%.

The

H63D/WT

and

WT/WT

groups

showed

similar

laboratory

profiles,

reinforcing

that

significant

hyperferritinemia

may

occur

even

in

the

absence

of

HFE

variants.

Ferritin

did

not

discriminate

genotypes

(p

=

0.465).

Zygosity

analysis

revealed

a

trend

toward

higher

ferritin

in

homozygotes

(p

=

0.057)

and

marked

differences

in

transferrin

saturation

(p

<

0.001).

Magnetic

resonance

imaging

showed

severe

hepatic

iron

overload

predominantly

in

C282Y

homozygotes.


Conclusion:

The

findings

of

this

study

expand

the

understanding

of

hyperferritinemia

in

our

population,

being

largely

consistent

with

the

international

literature,

particularly

regarding

the

greater

clinical

expressivity

in

men

and

the

association

between

C282Y

homozygosity

and

elevated

ferritin

and

transferrin

saturation.

However,

relevant

differences

emerged

when

compared

with

European

studies,

such

as

the

greater

phenotypic

expressivity

of

genotypes

10

involving

the

H63D

mutation—even

in

simple

heterozygotes—and

the

identification

of

pathogenic

variants

in

patients

with

transferrin

saturation

below

40%.

These

particularities

may

reflect

the

diverse

genetic

background

of

southern

Brazil,

as

well

as

environmental

and

cultural

influences.

Thus,

the

results

reinforce

the

need

for

a

more

sensitive

and

integrated

clinical

and

laboratory

evaluation

when

hereditary

hemochromatosis

is

suspected,

in

order

to

reduce

underdiagnosis

and

appropriately

guide

clinical

management.lights

the

need

for

integrated,

sensitive

diagnostic

strategies

adapted

to

the

local

context.

Introduction:

Hyperferritinemia

is

a

frequent

finding

in

clinical

practice

and

has

diverse

etiologies,

ranging

from

inflammatory

and

metabolic

processes

to

true

genetic

iron

overload,

such

as

hereditary

hemochromatosis

(HH).

In

Brazil,

ethnic

heterogeneity

and

regional

variation

in

the

prevalence

of

HFE

gene

mutations

may

modify

the

phenotypic

expression

of

the

disease,

making

it

essential

to

understand

how

laboratory

markers

and

genotypes

behave

in

admixed

populations.


Objective:

This

study

aimed

to

describe

the

clinical,

laboratory,

and

genetic

profile

of

patients

investigated

between

2010

and

2024

for

suspected

iron

overload

at

a

university

hospital

in

southern

Brazil,

analyzing

differences

between

carriers

and

non-carriers

of

HFE

mutations,

comparing

genotypes

and

zygosity

patterns,

and

assessing

the

influence

of

sex

on

laboratory

outcomes.


Methods:

This

was

a

retrospective

study

including

278

patients

investigated

between

2010

and

2024.

Demographic

variables,

laboratory

parameters,

comorbidities,

and

HFE

genotypes

were

analyzed.

Comparisons

were

performed

according

to

sex,

mutation

type,

and

zygosity

pattern

using

non-parametric

tests.


Results:

Among

the

individuals

evaluated,

54%

carried

an

HFE

mutation,

with

the

most

frequent

genotypes

being

H63D/WT

(23.7%)

and

C282Y/C282Y

(10.8%).

Men

were

diagnosed

earlier

(55

vs.

60

years;

p

<

0.01)

and

had

significantly

higher

ferritin

levels

(950

vs.

609

ng/mL;

p

=

0.03).

C282Y

homozygosity

exhibited

the

most

expressive

phenotype,

with

a

median

transferrin

saturation

of

88%.

The

H63D/WT

and

WT/WT

groups

showed

similar

laboratory

profiles,

reinforcing

that

significant

hyperferritinemia

may

occur

even

in

the

absence

of

HFE

variants.

Ferritin

did

not

discriminate

genotypes

(p

=

0.465).

Zygosity

analysis

revealed

a

trend

toward

higher

ferritin

in

homozygotes

(p

=

0.057)

and

marked

differences

in

transferrin

saturation

(p

<

0.001).

Magnetic

resonance

imaging

showed

severe

hepatic

iron

overload

predominantly

in

C282Y

homozygotes.


Conclusion:

The

findings

of

this

study

expand

the

understanding

of

hyperferritinemia

in

our

population,

being

largely

consistent

with

the

international

literature,

regarding

the

greater

clinical

expressivity

in

the

association

between

C282Y

homozygosity

and

elevated

ferritin

and

transferrin

saturation.

mutation—even

variants

transferrin

saturation

below

40%.

particularities

reflect

the

diverse

genetic

background

of

southern

Brazil,

as

well

as

environmental

and

cultural

influences.

Thus,

the

results

reinforce

the

need

for

a

more

sensitive

and

integrated

clinical

and

laboratory

evaluation

when

hereditary

hemochromatosis

is

suspected,

reduce

underdiagnosis

appropriately

guide

management.lights

strategies

⁺

e

na

processos

e

nos

e

órgãos.

O

dietético

é

o

heme,

em

de

animal

aves

e

e

o

não

de

vegetal,

na

férrica.

principal

fonte

de

absorvível

na

humana

é

o

heme,

que

de

80%

do

absorvido,

devido

à

sua

maior

biodisponibilidade

(3,4).

do

é

principalmente

regulada

interação

entre

a

hepcidina,

um

hormônio

hepático,

e

a

ferroportina,

a

principal

proteína

exportadora

de

ferro.

proteína

HFE

(codificada

pelo

gene

HFE),

na

superfície

dos

interage

com

a

diférrica

(Tf-Fe²)

e

com

os

receptores

de

transferrina

(TFR2).

os

níveis

de

aumentam,

do

complexo

e

que

ativa

a

de

a

a

síntese

de

de

fisiológica

(3

a

4

g).

A

ferritina,

principal

proteína

de

do

de

forma

as

desse

possa

se

comportar

como

reagente

de

fase

aguda.

produção

insuficiente

de

à

hiperabsorção

crônica

de

desse

metal

8,

9).

de

livre

⁺
